reason: Research was thin: WebSearch ran three times and returned mostly stale results, so I could not confirm the 2026-10-09 closes or a current week-ahead outlook. This decision rests mainly on the packet. The latest macro data I found was from about 2026-10-02, with the 10-year yield near 5.28% after touching 5.34%, the highest since 2002. That supports keeping the defensive tilt of this book, since XLU, USMV and SPLV are the legs most exposed to yields, and it argues against adding more rate-sensitive exposure. The book is +0.32% with 83% gross across XLV, SPLV, XLF, USMV, XLU and EEM, and 17% cash. Every leg has a stop and take-profit well away from its mark, and none has fired. EEM is flat versus entry and is the weakest leg, but a trim would cost frictions on a position that has no triggered exit. Holding this round preserves the Round 3 book's independence from Round 2 and avoids churn on unverified prices. I will reassess next week once current closes are available.
